cosy-lesson.title: "The older you get the more you understand why people disappear with art, music, books and quiet living.": Anonymous

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Quiet ≠ noisy – making little or no noise; peaceful and calm.

p.em: Example: I enjoy a quiet morning with a cup of warm tea.

cosy-blockquote.p: Disappear ≠ appear – to go away to a place where you cannot be seen or found.

p.em: Example: He likes to disappear into his study to read historical novels.

cosy-blockquote.p: Relax ≠ stress – to rest and become less active or worried.

p.em: Example: Soft instrumental music helps me relax after work.

cosy-blockquote.p: Hobby ≠ duty – an activity that you do for pleasure in your free time.

p.em: Example: Painting watercolor landscapes is my favorite weekend hobby.

cosy-blockquote.p: Peaceful ≠ chaotic – calm and quiet, without violence or noise.

p.em: Example: Walking in the park gives me a peaceful feeling.

cosy-blockquote.p: Prefer – to like one thing or person better than another.

p.em: Example: Many adults prefer staying home to going to loud parties.

cosy-blockquote.p: Routine ≠ chaos – a regular series of movements or actions.

p.em: Example: Reading before bed is a healthy evening routine.

cosy-blockquote.p: Simple ≠ complex – easy to understand, do, or use; uncluttered.

p.em: Example: A simple lifestyle often brings great personal happiness.

cosy-blockquote.p: Comfort ≠ hardship – a state of physical ease and freedom from pain or constraint.

p.em: Example: Reading a book on a comfortable sofa gives me great joy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Solitude ≠ crowd – the state of being alone, especially when this is pleasant.

p.em: Example: Artists often need quiet solitude to create good paintings.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Why do people often choose a quiet activity after a busy work week?
★ Do you agree that the more art you observe, the happier you feel?

How does listening to music help us relax when we feel stressed?
★ What kind of music helps you relax the best?

Why do many adults prefer staying home rather than going to crowded places?
★ Do you prefer loud parties or quiet coffee meetings?

How can having a creative hobby improve our everyday mood?
★ What hobby would you like to try in the future?

What makes a room or garden feel truly peaceful?
★ Where do you go when you want a peaceful moment?

How does a steady morning routine help us start the day well?
★ What is one simple step in your morning routine?

Why are simple pleasures like reading often the most comforting?
★ What is one simple thing that made you smile this week?

How does art bring comfort to people when they are feeling sad?
★ Do you have a favorite painting, book, or movie that gives you comfort?

Why is some quiet solitude good for our mental well-being?
★ How many hours of quiet time do you like to have each day?

Why do some people like to disappear into a good story for a few hours?
★ What book or movie made you forget time recently?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our quiet habits and evening routines.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our quiet habits and evening routines.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, more people will work remotely to enjoy quiet living in small towns. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you like to live in a quiet village or a big city in ten years?

Digital screens make it harder for children to enjoy simple physical books. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you read paper books or digital e-readers more often?

Every worker should have one hour of guaranteed solitude during the workday. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How would you spend one hour of quiet time at work?

High-tech headphones allow us to relax anywhere, even in noisy subway trains. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you use noise-canceling headphones when traveling?

People will always prefer human-made art over machine-generated pictures. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Can computer art feel as emotional as handmade art?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation with teacher in 1-on-1 format.

ul.li: Incorrect: I am more old than before. → Correct: I am older than before. ((Short adjectives take '-er' ending: older, not 'more old'.))
Incorrect: I like quietly places. → Correct: I like quiet places. ((Use the adjective 'quiet' to modify nouns like 'places', not the adverb 'quietly'.))
Incorrect: It help me to relaxed. → Correct: It helps me to relax / It helps me relax. ((Use the base verb 'relax' after 'to' or directly after 'help'.))
